answer: For standard reimbursement claims, you must submit the claim within 30 days of discharge [1][2]. However, an archived source conflicts with this by stating the deadline is 15 days from the date of discharge [3]. Additionally, for Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the reimbursement submission window is 60 days from discharge [5].
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3][4].
Maternity cover is not available on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1]. Under the Bronze plan terms and sub-limits, maternity is explicitly listed as not covered [2].

Pre-existing conditions carry a 36-month waiting period on retail plans unless Aurora explicitly waives it in writing on the policy schedule [3][5]. Under the Aurora Senior Care plan, the waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 24 months [5].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1]. Under Aurora Life policies, the grace period for an annual premium mode is also 30 days [5].

Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns as of 1 April 2026 [1]. The authoritative list is maintained in the Aurora app and on the portal, as hospitals join and leave the network continuously [1].

The no-claim bonus for Aurora Gold is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating to a maximum of 100% [1][5]. The bonus is not reduced if a claim is made; it only stops accumulating for that year [1].
IVF and assisted reproduction are listed under permanent treatment-related exclusions [1]. Therefore, you cannot claim for IVF treatment [1].
Under the Aurora Gold plan, the sub-limit for cataract surgery is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome or receive no response within 15 days, you can escalate to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2]. If Aurora's final response is unsatisfactory or they have not responded within 30 days of the original complaint, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].

All plans include road ambulance cover of ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1]. Additionally, the Aurora Gold plan provides air ambulance cover up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India on prior authorisation [5].

In-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The standard 30-day initial waiting period applies, and no separate waiting period is required [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3]. A new policyholder may cancel within 15 days of receiving the policy document, or 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. Upon cancellation, the policyholder receives a refund of premium less proportionate risk premium for the period of cover, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
You earn 150 wellness points per year for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a medical procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advances, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment does not qualify as a day-care procedure [3].
For an emergency admission under the cashless route, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1][5].
Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a Third Party Administrator (TPA) [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, not everything will be paid because the room-rent limit for a Silver plan with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured is 2%, or ₹10,000 per day [1][2]. Because the ₹15,000 per day room exceeds this limit, an eligibility ratio of 0.667 applies and proportionate deductions will be made across applicable hospitalisation charges [1][5].

Dependent parents can be covered under the Silver plan (at an extra premium), Gold plan, and Platinum plan, but cannot be added to the Bronze plan [1]. Adding a parent changes the premium calculation, as policy premium is determined by the age of the eldest covered member [4]. Aurora advisers are required to present both the floater addition and an individual senior-citizen policy option in writing before the sale [4].

Waiting periods already served with a previous insurer carry over on portability only up to the sum insured of the previous policy, including any accrued no-claim bonus [1][2]. Any increase or excess in sum insured will be subject to fresh waiting periods on the incremental amount [1][2].

To continue cover beyond the first 90 days, you must inform Aurora within 90 days of birth to add the newborn to the policy as a dependent [1]. Adding the newborn within this 90-day window is guaranteed-issue with no medical underwriting, whereas after this period the child is treated as a fresh applicant [1].
The out-patient benefit (OPD rider) is not available on the Bronze plan [1]. I don't have enough information in the provided sources to answer that.
Under the Aurora Silver plan, a claim in any year reduces your accumulated no-claim bonus by 10 percentage points [1]. It does not reset your bonus to zero [1].
Under the Gold plan, the limit for a Caesarean section is ₹1,00,000 per delivery [1]. I don't have enough information in the provided sources to answer that.

Knee joint replacement other than following an accident is not covered immediately, as it is subject to a 24-month waiting period [1][5]. However, if the procedure follows an accident, accidental injury coverage is available immediately from day one [1][2][5].
Total discounts are capped at 30% of the base premium [1]. The wellness discount, which is up to 15% at renewal, is applied last after the cap and is the only discount that may exceed it [1][3][5].

Cashless access is denied if the hospital is an excluded provider [2][4]. You may seek reimbursement instead [5], but the sources conflict on the eligibility conditions: Source [1] states that reimbursement is payable only if the admission was a genuine emergency and no alternative facility was reachable [1], whereas Source [3] states that reimbursement is available with pre-approval [3].

For a reimbursement claim, you have 45 days from the date of the query to respond [2][5]. For an Aurora motor insurance claim, the deadline to respond to a query is 30 days from the date of the query [4].

Under current guidelines, a planned cashless admission must be notified at least 72 hours before admission [2][3]. However, an archived source states the deadline is 48 hours before admission, meaning the sources conflict [1].

Aurora settles or rejects a complete reimbursement claim within 15 working days of receiving the last required document [1][2]. However, an archived source conflicts with this, stating the timeline is 30 days from the last document [3].
Aurora Gold has no co-payment at any age [1]. Aurora Silver has no co-payment when the eldest insured member is below 60 years of age [2].

Across Aurora's four plans, pre-hospitalisation coverage is 30 days, 45 days, 60 days, and 90 days [1][3]. The post-hospitalisation coverage across the four plans is 60 days, 90 days, 120 days, and 180 days [1].

Dependent parents-in-law can be covered under the Gold and Platinum plans [1]. The Gold plan explicitly removes room-rent and ICU sub-limits [3]. Therefore, the Gold plan provides coverage for parents-in-law without a room-rent sub-limit [1][3].

Dental treatment and oral surgery are permanently excluded from all Aurora indemnity plans, unless necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [2][3]. Out-patient dental work is also listed as not covered by any plan [1].

Denial of cashless access is not a rejection of your claim [1]. In cases where cashless was denied, you can file for reimbursement under Route 2 [3].
